style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The great psalm of benefits, and Scripture's warmest sustained meditation on the mercy of God. David begins by preaching to himself -- Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not -- because gratitude's great enemy is not doubt but amnesia. Then the benefits are counted like coins: iniquities forgiven, diseases healed, life redeemed from the pit, a crown of covenant love and deep compassion, good things until youth renews like the eagle's. At the psalm's center stands the LORD's own self-description from Sinai -- merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in covenant love (Exodus 34:6) -- and around it the measurements no line can survey: mercy high as the heavens are above the earth, transgressions removed as far as east is from west, compassion like a father's over his children. The tenderest verse may be 14: He knows our frame, He remembers that we are dust -- our frailty is not His disappointment but His consideration. Man's days are grass, and the wind's one pass ends them; but the chesed of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear Him. The psalm that began with one soul commanding itself ends conducting the universe -- angels, hosts, and every work in every place of His dominion -- before returning home to the first pew: Bless the LORD, O my soul.

1.text: Of David. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and everything within me, bless His holy name!
1.amp: A Psalm of David. Bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH], O my soul [nephesh]: and all that is within [qereb] me, bless His holy [qodesh] name [shem].
1.notes: barak (H1288): the creature blessing the Creator -- returning honor for benefit. The summons is to the nephesh (H5315) and every qereb (H7130), all the inward parts: no faculty left in the pews. David is his own worship leader here, the soul commanded, not consulted.

2.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget one of all His benefits:
2.amp: Bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH], O my soul [nephesh], and forget [shakach] not all His benefits [gemul -- His dealings, His deserved recompense]:
2.notes: The enemy of praise is shakach (H7911), forgetting -- not disbelief but drift. gemul (H1576) is what one is dealt: the psalm now itemizes the account so memory has handles, five participles of grace in the next three verses.

3.text: who forgives all your twisted guilt, who heals all your diseases,
3.amp: Who forgives [salach] all your iniquities [avon]; who heals [rapha] all your diseases [tachalu];
3.notes: First and deepest benefit: salach (H5545), the forgiveness-verb used only of God in Scripture, covering kol avon (H5771), all of it. rapha (H7495) is the LORD's own name for Himself at Marah (cf. Exodus 15:26) -- healer of body and soul in whatever order and time He appoints.

4.text: who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with covenant love and deep compassions,
4.amp: Who redeems [gaal -- ransoms as Kinsman-Redeemer] your life [chay] from destruction [shachat -- the pit]; who crowns [atar -- encircles as with a crown] you with lovingkindness [chesed -- covenant love] and tender mercies [rachamim -- womb-deep compassions];
4.notes: gaal (H1350) is the kinsman-redeemer's verb, Boaz's word: redemption by a relative who pays in person. Pulled from the shachat (H7845), the pit, the ransomed man is then atar (H5849), crowned -- a beggar from the pit wearing chesed and rachamim (H2617, H7356) for a diadem.

5.text: who satisfies your years with good things, so that your youth renews itself like the eagle's.
5.amp: Who satisfies [saba] your mouth ['your ornament, your prime', adi, the KJV margin] with good [tov] things; so that your youth [neurim] is renewed [chadash] like the eagle's [nesher].
5.notes: The fifth benefit: saba (H7646), satisfaction, filled with tov. The nesher (H5404) molts and returns to full feather and force -- strength renewed at the age when strength should fail (cf. Isaiah 40:31). chadash (H2318) is the renewing-verb of Psalm 51:10.

6.text: The LORD works righteousness and justice for all who are pressed down and oppressed.
6.amp: The LORD [YHWH] executes [asah] righteousness [tsedaqah] and judgment [mishpat] for all that are oppressed [ashaq -- the exploited, the extorted].
6.notes: From personal benefits to public character: tsedaqah and mishpat (H6666, H4941) worked -- asah, done, not merely decreed -- for the ashuqim (H6231), everyone ground down by power. The God of my forgiveness is also the God of their justice.

7.text: He made His ways known to Moses, His mighty deeds to the children of Israel.
7.amp: He made known [yada] His ways [derek] unto Moses [Mosheh], His acts [alilah -- His deeds] unto the children [ben] of Israel [Yisrael].
7.notes: A distinction inside the revelation: Israel saw the alilot (H5949), the acts -- sea split, bread from the sky; Moses was shown the derek (H1870), the ways, the character behind the acts (cf. Exodus 33:13). The next verse quotes exactly what Moses learned there.

8.text: The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and great in covenant love.
8.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is merciful [rachum -- compassionate] and gracious [channun], slow [arek] to anger [aph], and plenteous ['great in mercy', rav chesed, the KJV margin].
8.notes: Sinai's self-revelation quoted nearly verbatim (cf. Exodus 34:6), the verse Israel repeated more than any other about its God: rachum, channun (H7349, H2587), arek aph -- literally 'long of nose', anger on the longest fuse -- and rav chesed, covenant love in bulk. This is the psalm's center of gravity.

9.text: He will not always press the charge, nor keep His anger on guard forever.
9.amp: He will not always [netsach] chide [rib -- contend, press the lawsuit]: neither will He keep [natar -- guard, nurse] His anger for ever [olam].
9.notes: rib (H7378) is courtroom contention: God will not prosecute in perpetuity. natar (H5201) is to keep watch over something -- the grudge-nursing He refuses; His anger is real but has a term, His chesed has none (cf. Isaiah 57:16; Micah 7:18).

10.text: He has not treated us as our sins deserved, nor paid us back in the coin of our iniquities.
10.amp: He has not dealt [asah] with us after our sins [chet]; nor rewarded [gamal -- repaid] us according to our iniquities [avon].
10.notes: The verse every honest conscience countersigns: the gemul-root of verse 2 returns as gamal (H1580) -- the 'benefits' we received are precisely NOT the repayment we earned. Between our chet (H2399) and His response stands a mercy that broke the equivalence -- at a cross (cf. 2 Corinthians 5:21).

11.text: For as high as the heavens stand over the earth, so towering is His covenant love over those who fear Him.
11.amp: For as the heaven [shamayim] is high [gabah] above the earth [eretz], so great [gabar -- mighty, prevailing] is His mercy [chesed] toward them that fear [yare] Him.
11.notes: The first of three measurements: vertical. gabah (H1361) and gabar (H1396) -- as the sky towers, so His chesed prevails, love measured in light-years and still underestimated. The recipients are the yare (H3373), those who fear Him: reverence is the container the mercy fills.

12.text: As far as the east is from the west, that far has He removed our transgressions from us.
12.amp: As far as [rachaq] the east [mizrach] is from the west [maarab], so far has He removed [rachaq] our transgressions [pesha] from us.
12.notes: The second measurement: horizontal, and infinite by design -- travel north and you eventually head south, but east (H4217) never becomes west; the distance never closes. rachaq (H7368) twice: the removal is as final as the geometry. Our pesha (H6588), the rebellions themselves, carried off beyond recall (cf. Isaiah 38:17; Micah 7:19).

13.text: As a father holds his children in compassion, so the LORD holds in compassion those who fear Him.
13.amp: Like as a father [ab] pities [racham -- has womb-deep compassion on] his children [ben], so the LORD [YHWH] pities [racham] them that fear [yare] Him.
13.notes: The third measure is not distance but kinship: racham (H7355), compassion from the deepest inward place, the father bending to the child who cannot reach the counter. Jesus built His whole doctrine of prayer on this analogy (cf. Matthew 7:11; Luke 15:20).

14.text: For He knows the way we are formed; He keeps in mind that we are dust.
14.amp: For He knows [yada] our frame [yetser -- how we were formed, our molding]; He remembers [zakar] that we are dust [afar].
14.notes: yetser (H3336) is the potter's word, from the forming of Adam (cf. Genesis 2:7): He knows the clay because He shaped it. zakar afar (H2142, H6083) -- the Maker keeps our composition in mind; our frailty draws His consideration, not His contempt. The most comforting anthropology in Scripture.

15.text: As for man, his days are like the grass; like a flower of the open field, so he blossoms --
15.amp: As for man [enosh -- frail mortal man], his days [yom] are as grass [chatsir]: as a flower [tsits] of the field [sadeh], so he flourishes [tsuts].
15.notes: enosh (H582), man in his mortality, in the grass-and-flower figure of Psalm 90:5-6 and Isaiah 40:6-8. The tsits (H6731) of the open sadeh is glorious and utterly exposed -- no gardener, no wall, one season.

16.text: for a wind passes over it, and it is gone, and its own place no longer recognizes it.
16.amp: For the wind [ruach] passes over [abar] it, and it is gone ['it is not', the KJV margin]; and the place [maqom] thereof shall know [nakar -- recognize] it no more.
16.notes: One pass of the ruach (H7307) -- the hot east wind -- and the Hebrew says simply 'it is not'. nakar (H5234): even the maqom (H4725), the ground it grew from, cannot recognize where it stood. Mortality stated without cushion, so verse 17's 'but' can carry full weight.

17.text: But the covenant love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him, and His righteousness reaches to children's children,
17.amp: But the mercy [chesed -- covenant love] of the LORD [YHWH] is from everlasting [olam] to everlasting upon them that fear [yare] Him, and His righteousness [tsedaqah] unto children's children [ben];
17.notes: The great 'but' of the psalm: against grass-brief man stands chesed me-olam ad-olam (H5769) -- the same double-everlasting that measured God Himself in Psalm 90:2 now measures His love. And it runs forward, tsedaqah (H6666) to grandchildren: the covenant outlives every flower it covers.

18.text: to those who keep His covenant, and remember His precepts in order to do them.
18.amp: To such as keep [shamar] His covenant [berith], and to those that remember [zakar] His commandments [piqqud -- precepts] to do [asah] them.
18.notes: The everlasting love has a household: berith-keepers (H1285). zakar (H2142) answers verse 2's shakach -- the God who remembers we are dust asks that we remember His precepts, and remembering here has hands: 'to DO them' (asah, H6213).

19.text: The LORD has fixed His throne firm in the heavens, and His kingdom rules over everything that is.
19.amp: The LORD [YHWH] has prepared [kun -- established, made firm] His throne [kisse] in the heavens [shamayim]; and His kingdom [malkuth] rules [mashal] over all.
19.notes: The foundation under every promise so far: a kisse (H3678) kun (H3559), a throne fixed and firm, with malkuth (H4438) over kol -- all, no exceptions clause. The Father of verse 13 is also the King of everything; the compassion has omnipotence behind it.

20.text: Bless the LORD, you His angels, mighty in strength, who carry out His word, obedient to the voice of His word.
20.amp: Bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH], ye His angels [malak], that excel in strength ['mighty in strength', gibbor koach, the KJV margin], that do [asah] His commandments [dabar], hearkening [shama] unto the voice [qol] of His word [dabar].
20.notes: The doxology begins recruiting upward: malakim (H4397) who are gibbor koach (H1368, H3581), warriors of strength, whose obedience is instant -- shama at the qol of His dabar. One soul's praise now conscripts beings who outrank it.

21.text: Bless the LORD, all His hosts, His ministers who perform His pleasure.
21.amp: Bless [barak] ye the LORD [YHWH], all ye His hosts [tsaba -- armies]; ye ministers [sharath] of His, that do [asah] His pleasure [ratson].
21.notes: Wider still: the tsaba (H6635), the armies of heaven entire, described as sharath (H8334), sanctuary-ministers -- warriors whose warfare is worship, executing His ratson (H7522), His good pleasure.

22.text: Bless the LORD, all His works, in every place of His dominion. Bless the LORD, O my soul!
22.amp: Bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH], all His works [maaseh] in all places [maqom] of His dominion [memshalah]: bless the LORD, O my soul [nephesh].
22.notes: The circle completes at cosmic width -- kol maaseh (H4639), every made thing, in every maqom of the memshalah (H4475) -- and then returns deliberately to the one small voice that started it: barak YHWH, O my nephesh. The universe may sing, but David will not let his own soul stand silent in the choir.
